title: Wine Club: Loki’s Monthly Wine Social
description:
SOLD OUT

Loki Wine Club: Your New Friday-Night Wine Ritual

Bring a bottle, discover something unexpected and spend Friday evening sharing wine with a room full of fellow wine lovers.

Sometimes, Friday night calls for a glass of wine. And sometimes, you want that glass to come with good company, a little education and the chance to try something completely unexpected.

That is exactly what Loki Wine Club is for.

This relaxed monthly gathering is for people who believe wine is best enjoyed with others. Each guest helps shape the evening by bringing a bottle of wine from home or choosing one from Loki’s shelves. One of our Loki wine experts will host the evening, guide the group through the wines and help uncover the stories, regions, producers and winemaking ideas behind whatever appears on the table.

Together, we will open a collection of bottles, share them around and see where the evening takes us. It is not a formal wine class: there are no tests, no pressure and nobody will ask you to deliver tasting notes in front of the room.

You are very welcome to come on your own, and you do not need to know anybody before you arrive. The whole idea is to meet fellow wine lovers, discover something new and enjoy bottles that are much more fun when opened with other people.

How it works?

  • Bring a bottle you love, something interesting, or something you’d like to learn more about, no corkage fee
  • Share your bottle with the group and taste wines brought by other guests
  • Not sure what to choose? Simply buy your ticket and turn up. Arrive around 10–15 minutes early and we can help you choose something from Loki’s shelves.
  • There is no corkage fee, whether you bring your own bottle or buy one in-store
  • Enjoy a guided introduction and informal discussion led by our in-house expert
  • Discover a wonderfully unpredictable collection of bottles each month
  • Hear the story behind each wine — and share your own, if you would like to
  • Learn from our Loki wine expert and the other wine lovers around the table
  • Taste, share and discuss wine in a relaxed setting with no rigid structure
  • Meet new people in a friendly, welcoming atmosphere
  • Suitable for everyone, whatever your level of wine knowledge

What Should You Bring?

There is no prescribed theme and no bottle budget.

You could bring:

  • A £15 bottle you have recently discovered and absolutely love
  • Something unusual that you would like to understand better
  • A special bottle you have been saving for an occasion that never quite came up
  • An older bottle gathering dust at home that you received as a gift.
  • Something extravagant you have always wanted to share with people who will appreciate it

Perhaps you bought a bottle years ago for a special dinner, but the occasion never arrived. Perhaps the people you planned to open it with have since stopped drinking. This is your opportunity to finally pull the cork and share it with a room full of curious wine lovers.

There is no upper price limit and no pressure to impress. If you are not sure about your bottle, simply drop us an email and we will advise.

Wine Club Rules

  • No pressure to impress, although we may have to turn you down if you bring Blossom Hill, sorry..
  • Know your wine and want to tell everyone the story behind your bottle? Please do. We would love to hear about it.
  • Know absolutely nothing about it and would rather let someone else do the talking? That is completely fine too.
  • Our Loki expert, Melissa, will guide the tasting, talk us through the bottles and help everyone understand what they are drinking. Of course, anyone who thinks they can bring something capable of puzzling her is very welcome to try!
  • The evening is informal and conversational. We will open the bottles, pour them around, compare what everyone has brought and enjoy a completely unpredictable selection of wines together.
  • No two Wine Club evenings will ever be quite the same — because the wines are chosen by you.

Who Is Wine Club For?

    • Anyone looking for a more interesting way to spend a Friday evening over wine
    • People who love wine but do not necessarily know all the technical language
    • Experienced wine drinkers with bottles and stories they would like to share
    • Curious drinkers who want to expand their knowledge without attending a structured class
    • Anyone who enjoys discovering new wines through conversation and sharing
    • Solo guests who would like to meet other wine lovers
    • Anyone with a special, unusual or mysterious bottle waiting to be opened
    • Regulars who want to build a monthly wine ritual, and newcomers just as welcome

When: 6pm
Duration: 2 hours
Where: Loki Great Western Arcade
What to bring: A bottle to share — or arrive early and choose one with our help

title: Across the Alps: Austria & Germany Wine Tasting
description:
Neighbours on the map but wonderfully different in the glass, Austria and Germany produce some of Europe’s most elegant, food-friendly, and age-worthy wines. This special tasting invites you to compare these two remarkable wine nations side by side, discovering how climate, grape varieties, and winemaking traditions create distinct personalities on either side of the border.

From world-class Riesling and Grüner Veltliner to vibrant Pinot Noir and rich Blaufränkisch, you’ll taste seven carefully selected wines that showcase the very best each country has to offer. Along the way, our expert host will explore the similarities, the differences, and the fascinating history that has shaped these neighbouring wine regions.

Whether you’re already a fan of crisp aromatic whites or keen to discover Austria’s exciting reds and Germany’s hidden gems, this promises to be an engaging evening full of comparisons, conversation, and outstanding wines.

What to Expect at Our Austria vs Germany Wine Tasting

  • Taste seven premium wines from Austria and Germany
  • Compare classic grape varieties including Riesling, Grüner Veltliner, Pinot Noir, and Blaufränkisch
  • Discover how climate, soils, and regional traditions influence style
  • Learn the differences between Austrian and German winemaking philosophies
  • Explore both famous appellations and lesser-known regions
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance in a relaxed, sociable atmosphere

Example Wines You Might Taste

  • German Sekt – elegant traditional-method sparkling wine with crisp citrus, green apple, and fine mousse.
  • Wachau Grüner Veltliner – Austria’s flagship white, offering white pepper, orchard fruit, and vibrant minerality.
  • Mosel Riesling Kabinett – delicate, slate-driven Riesling balancing bright acidity with subtle fruit sweetness.
  • Kamptal Riesling – dry, focused, and beautifully structured with citrus, stone fruit, and mineral precision.
  • German Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir) – silky and refined with red cherry fruit, gentle spice, and elegant tannins.
  • Burgenland Blaufränkisch – Austria’s signature red, combining dark berries, peppery spice, and fresh acidity.
  • Beerenauslese or Trockenbeerenauslese – a luxurious sweet finale showcasing Germany or Austria’s mastery of noble-rot dessert wines.

(The final line-up may vary depending on availability, but every tasting is carefully curated to showcase the unique character and diversity of these two outstanding wine-producing countries.)

Who Should Join the Austria vs Germany Wine Tasting?

  • Lovers of crisp, aromatic white wines
  • Riesling and Grüner Veltliner enthusiasts looking to compare the classics
  • Wine lovers curious about cool-climate viticulture
  • Anyone keen to discover Austria’s exciting reds alongside Germany’s elegant Pinot Noir
  • Beginners and experienced tasters alike — informative, approachable, and packed with flavour

title: Cheese and Wine Tasting at City Centre
description:
Join us at Loki Great Western Arcade for our most popular event: the Cheese and Wine Tasting. Spend a Saturday afternoon discovering both timeless classics and exciting new pairings in a fun, relaxed, and educational setting.

Guided by one of Loki’s expert hosts, you’ll taste seven wines from our curated collection, each paired with an artisan cheese sourced from our favourite suppliers. Along the way, we’ll explore why some matches work so well, uncover surprising combinations, and prove that Port isn’t the only wine worth serving with cheese.

What to Expect at Our Cheese and Wine Tasting

  • Sample seven wines, each carefully matched to an artisan cheese
  • Learn how acidity, tannin, sweetness, and texture all play a role in pairing
  • Explore classic duos alongside creative and intriguing combinations
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere
  • Discover pairings that will inspire your next cheeseboard

Who Should Join the Cheese and Wine Tasting?

  • Cheese enthusiasts looking for perfect pairings
  • Wine lovers eager to discover new flavour combinations
  • Anyone who enjoys a relaxed, sociable tasting experience
  • Beginners and seasoned tasters alike – the event is accessible, delicious, and insightful

Six Cheese & Wine Tastings to Explore

We currently have six different volumes of our Cheese & Wine Tasting, each with its own selection of wines, cheeses and flavour combinations. So, if you have joined us before, your next tasting will not necessarily be the same. Simply book a different volume and enjoy a fresh set of pairings.

Below, you’ll find a sample pairings from each volume.

Volume 1 – Classic Cheese & Wine Pairings

The perfect introduction to cheese and wine matching. Discover some of the world’s most iconic combinations, from crisp Sauvignon Blanc with goat’s cheese to the timeless partnership of Port and Stilton. These are the pairings every cheese and wine lover should experience at least once. The wines and cheeses may vary from event to event, but the focus will always remain on classic combinations.

  • Fino Sherry with Manchego Curado
  • Sauvignon Blanc (Loire) with Crottin de Chavignol
  • White Burgundy with Délice de Bourgogne
  • Beaujolais Cru with Saint-Nectaire
  • Rioja Reserva with Mature Cheddar
  • Amarone della Valpolicella with Aged Gouda
  • Vintage Port with Stilton

Volume 2 – Sparkling & White-Led Pairings

A celebration of the wines that often pair best with cheese. While red wine often steals the spotlight, many cheeses truly shine alongside sparkling and white wines. Expect crisp acidity, mineral-driven whites and elegant reds that highlight texture and flavour in surprising ways. The exact wines and cheeses may change, but each tasting follows a progression from refreshing styles through to fuller-bodied wines before finishing with a sweet finale.

  • Crémant de Loire with Baron Bigod
  • Albariño with Burrata
  • Dry Riesling with Raclette
  • Assyrtiko with Gruyère
  • Pinot Noir with Reblochon
  • Cabernet Franc (Loire) with Lincolnshire Poacher
  • Tokaji Late Harvest with Fourme d’Ambert

Volume 3 – Discovery Pairings

For adventurous wine lovers looking to discover something new. This tasting explores unexpected combinations, lesser-known regions and cheeses you may never have tried before. Along the way, you’ll also enjoy a premium Champagne pairing to show that the classics still have a place amongst the discoveries. The pairings will evolve throughout the year as we uncover exciting new wines and cheeses.

  • Pet Nat with Lincolnshire Poacher
  • Godello with Smoked Scamorza
  • Champagne Blanc de Blancs with 24-month Comté
  • Nerello Mascalese with Fiore Sardo
  • Mencía with Mahón Curado
  • Valpolicella Ripasso with Époisses
  • Jurançon Moelleux with Bleu des Causses

Volume 4 – Classic Dinner Party

A luxurious evening inspired by the perfect dinner party. Beginning with Champagne and finishing with a decadent dessert wine, this tasting follows the natural progression of an elegant meal. Refined, indulgent and packed with crowd-pleasing combinations. Wines and cheeses may vary, but the progression and style of the evening will remain the same.

  • Champagne with Brillat-Savarin
  • Chablis with Chaource
  • White Rhône with Tomme de Savoie
  • Burgundy Pinot Noir with Reblochon
  • Amarone della Valpolicella with Aged Gouda
  • Ribera del Duero Reserva with Lincolnshire Poacher
  • Pedro Ximénez with Stilton

Volume 5 – Playful Pairings

Fresh, vibrant and a little less traditional. Starting with rosé, this tasting explores lighter styles, aromatic whites, Alpine cheeses and a few unexpected combinations along the way. It’s designed to be relaxed, seasonal and full of delicious surprises. Pairings may change, but the playful spirit of the evening will always remain.

  • Sparkling Rosé with Baron Bigod
  • Picpoul de Pinet with Valencay
  • Gewürztraminer with Munster
  • Orange Wine with Manchego Curado
  • Jura Savagnin with Morbier
  • Frappato with Pecorino Toscano
  • Moscatel de Setúbal with Serra da Estrela

Volume 6 – Freestyle & New Discoveries

Our most flexible and ever-changing tasting. Built around exciting new arrivals, seasonal favourites and the best discoveries from our buying trips, no two editions are likely to be the same. Sometimes we’ll finish with a big red, sometimes with a sweet wine—but every event is designed to introduce you to something memorable. This is our most dynamic format, allowing us to showcase whatever we’re most excited about at the time.

  • English Traditional Method Sparkling with Tunworth
  • Txakoli with Burrata
  • Etna Bianco with Taleggio
  • Tavel Rosé with Morbier
  • Xinomavro with Fiore Sardo
  • Aglianico with Provolone del Monaco
  • Seasonal finale – either a sweet wine, fortified wine or flagship red depending on the theme

Event Details

When: 12pm
Duration: 2 hours
Where: Loki Great Western Arcade

*You can receive a full refund up to 30 days before the event and transfer your ticket up to 14 days before the event.
All transfers within 14 days of the event will incur a £10 fee per ticket to cover non-recoverable costs.

Images are for illustration purposes only.
address: Loki Great Western Arcade, 36 Great Western Arcade, Birmingham, B2 5HU

title: Come Drink With Me, by Amuse Booze
description:
Pack your best mood: you’re going on a drinks trip around the world with Amuse Booze, and you won’t know exactly where you’re heading until you arrive.

This fun, interactive tasting takes you through four different countries in 90 minutes, with each stop bringing its own spirit, culture, signature serve and perfectly paired nibble. One minute you could be embracing Italian aperitivo culture, the next sharing Pintxos in Barcelona, before heading to Jalisco for a Mexican fiesta.

And that is only the beginning.

With Japan, the Caribbean, USA, India, France and the UK also potentially on the itinerary, your host will reveal the evening’s four featured destinations as a surprise on the day. Every session is designed to feel a little different, so expect great drinks, fascinating stories, unexpected flavours and plenty of interaction along the way.

This isn’t a formal spirits lecture. It’s a lively journey through drinking cultures from around the world, exploring not just what people drink, but how, when and why they drink it.

About the Experience

Over four rounds, your host will transport you to a different country through a carefully chosen spirit and an interactive signature serve inspired by local drinking traditions.

You might discover the art of the Italian aperitivo, explore how agave spirits sit at the heart of Mexican culture, learn the rituals behind Japanese whisky or sake, or dive into the rum-soaked history of the Caribbean.

Each destination will also be paired with a small nibble inspired by the country or drinking occasion, bringing the whole experience together.

Along the way, expect fun facts, stories, simple cocktail techniques and plenty of surprises. You’ll learn without feeling like you’re in a classroom — and, most importantly, you’ll get to drink your way through the lesson.

What to Expect

  • Travel through 4 surprise countries in 90 minutes
  • Enjoy 4 premium spirits and interactive signature serves
  • Discover drinking traditions and cultures from around the world
  • Experience everything from aperitivo culture and tapas to tequila rituals and tropical serves
  • Enjoy a small paired nibble with each destination
  • Learn fun facts, local traditions and stories behind some of the world’s most famous drinks
  • Discover how different countries approach flavour, serving styles and social drinking
  • Get involved with interactive elements and signature serves along the way
  • Expect a different journey depending on the countries selected for your session
  • Relax, have fun and discover something you probably haven’t tried before

Where Could We Take You?

Your four destinations will remain a surprise until the day, but the passport could include:

  • Italy – aperitivo culture, bitters, vermouth and the art of the pre-dinner drink
  • Spain – Pintxos, tapas and sociable serves designed for sharing
  • Mexico – tequila, agave and a lively taste of Jalisco
  • Japan – precision, ritual and beautifully balanced drinking traditions
  • The Caribbean – rum, tropical flavours and centuries of island drinks culture
  • USA – bourbon, rye and classic American cocktail culture
  • India – aromatic spices, bold flavours and the fascinating rise of Indian spirits
  • France – elegant aperitifs, brandy and classic French drinking traditions
  • United Kingdom – gin, whisky and a few familiar favourites with an unexpected twist

The four featured countries and drinks will vary between sessions and will be revealed on the day. That is all part of the fun.

Who Is This For?

  • Anyone who loves cocktails, spirits and discovering new flavours
  • Curious drinkers who want something more interactive than a traditional tasting
  • Groups of friends looking for a fun and unusual experience
  • Cocktail lovers interested in the stories and cultures behind their favourite drinks
  • Wine drinkers wanting to explore the world of spirits
  • Anyone who enjoys travel, food and trying something new
  • Beginners are very welcome — no spirits knowledge required

Expect the Unexpected

You won’t receive the full drinks menu in advance. You won’t know exactly which countries you’re visiting. And that is very much the point!

Your host will reveal each destination as the journey unfolds, making every round a new experience and every tasting a little bit different.

Four countries. Four drinks. Four nibbles. Ninety minutes.

Where are we taking you? You’ll have to turn up to find out.

title: Fine Wine Tasting – Bordeaux
description:
Few regions embody the idea of fine wine quite like Bordeaux. Home to some of the world’s most celebrated châteaux and historic appellations, Bordeaux has built its reputation on wines of remarkable structure, elegance and longevity. This exclusive Fine Wine Bordeaux Tasting offers the opportunity to explore seven exceptional wines from across the region, with just 10 guests joining us for an intimate Friday evening experience.

The line-up has been carefully selected to showcase the extraordinary diversity of Bordeaux, travelling from the gravel soils of Pessac-Léognan through the great Left Bank appellations of Saint-Julien, Saint-Estèphe and Margaux, before crossing the Gironde to Saint-Émilion and Pomerol. The evening will conclude with the beautifully complex sweet wines of Sauternes.

Guided by one of Loki’s wine experts, you’ll explore how location, soil, grape variety, vintage and winemaking shape the individual character of each château. Compare the power and structure of Saint-Estèphe with the refinement of Margaux, discover the contrast between Cabernet Sauvignon-dominated Left Bank wines and the Merlot-led blends of the Right Bank, and experience a completely different expression of Bordeaux through its fine white and sweet wines.

With only ten places available, this tasting has been designed to offer a more personal and detailed experience than a traditional large-group event. There will be plenty of opportunity to discuss each wine, explore the stories behind these historic estates and understand why these châteaux have earned such distinguished reputations.

Expect prestigious estates, iconic Bordeaux appellations and seven outstanding wines in an evening created for anyone who would like to experience one of the world’s greatest wine regions at a truly exceptional level.

What to Expect at Our Bordeaux Fine Wine Tasting

  • Taste seven exceptional Bordeaux wines from some of the region’s most prestigious appellations
  • Strictly limited to just 10 guests for an intimate and exclusive Friday evening

title: Labels Off: A Blind Wine Tasting

Expect helpful hints, lively discussion and the occasional theory that sounds wonderfully convincing until the bottle is revealed.

You don’t need an encyclopaedic knowledge of wine to take part. Whether you’re confidently naming grape varieties or simply deciding that a wine smells like your favourite fruit, every observation adds to the fun. Compare notes with your fellow tasters, question your first impressions and see which clues lead you in the right direction.

As the identities are revealed, we’ll explore the stories behind the bottles and what made each wine taste the way it did. Expect a few surprises, plenty of laughs and some new favourites you might never have chosen by looking at the label.

  • Put your senses to the test in a relaxed and playful setting
  • Learn a simple approach to tasting wine blind

  • Make your guesses with helpful guidance from a Loki wine expert

title: Tot to Tiki, by Amuse Booze
description:
From sailors’ rations and sugar plantations to beach bars, Daiquiris and full-blown Tiki extravagance, rum has one of the most colourful stories in the drinks world.

Tot to Tiki by Amuse Booze takes you on a journey through that story, following rum from its early Caribbean beginnings to the remarkably diverse spirit we know today. Across four timeline-inspired serves, you’ll discover how one spirit evolved into three distinct traditions — Rum, Ron and Rhum — shaped by different islands, empires, ingredients and approaches to production.

Expect history without the history lesson, plenty of fascinating facts and four very different drinks designed to bring each chapter of the story to life.

Pirates may feature.

Tiny umbrellas are not guaranteed.

About the Experience

Across four rounds, your Amuse Booze host will take you through key moments in rum’s evolution, with each drink representing a different chapter in its story.

We’ll explore how sugarcane became spirit, why British, Spanish and French Caribbean islands developed such different styles, and how everything from naval traditions and colonial trade to Prohibition and post-war Tiki culture helped shape the way we drink rum today.

Along the way, you’ll discover the difference between molasses-based rum and fresh sugarcane Rhum Agricole, explore contrasting ageing and production styles, and taste how geography and history have created an extraordinary range of flavours.

Expect stories, interactive moments and plenty of Amuse Booze fun along the way.

What to Expect

  • Enjoy 4 timeline-inspired rum serves, each representing a key chapter in rum history
  • Travel from the earliest Caribbean spirits through naval rum, classic cocktails and the rise of Tiki culture
  • Discover the differences between Rum, Ron and Rhum
  • Explore British, Spanish and French-influenced rum traditions
  • Learn how molasses, fresh sugarcane juice, fermentation and ageing influence flavour
  • Discover how piracy, naval history, colonial trade and Caribbean culture became intertwined with rum
  • Taste a variety of styles, from bold and characterful to smooth, elegant and tropical
  • Pick up plenty of strange, surprising and genuinely useful rum facts
  • Experience an interactive tasting that’s informative without taking itself too seriously

Where Will the Journey Take You?

The exact drinks will form part of the experience, but your journey could include:

  • The Early Tot – exploring rum’s beginnings in the Caribbean and the fiery spirits that became part of everyday naval life
  • Rum – the British-influenced tradition, often associated with Jamaica, Barbados and other former British Caribbean islands, where richer and more characterful styles developed
  • Ron – the smoother Spanish-influenced tradition found in places such as Cuba, Puerto Rico and beyond, where ageing and blending helped create a more refined style
  • Rhum – the distinctive French Caribbean tradition, particularly Rhum Agricole, produced directly from fresh sugarcane juice rather than molasses
  • The Cocktail Revolution – how drinks such as the Daiquiri helped take Caribbean spirits around the world
  • Tiki Takes Over – tropical escapism, elaborate cocktails and the colourful mid-century drinking culture that turned rum into the star of the show

The final four drinks will be selected to tell the story of rum through the glass, so expect a few surprises along the way.

Who Is This For?

  • Rum lovers wanting to explore the spirit beyond their usual bottle
  • Cocktail fans curious about the history behind classic rum serves
  • Anyone who has wondered what actually separates Rum, Ron and Rhum
  • Curious drinkers who enjoy history when it comes with something good in the glass
  • Groups of friends looking for a fun and different tasting experience
  • Whisky or brandy drinkers interested in exploring aged rum
  • Complete beginners — no previous rum knowledge required

From Tot to Tiki

Rum’s story isn’t really one story at all.

It’s sailors and sugarcane. Pirates and plantations. Caribbean islands separated by language and empire. Naval rations, elegant Cuban cocktails and enormous Tiki creations decorated with enough fruit to qualify as lunch.

Tot to Tiki brings those stories together through four drinks, four moments in time and plenty of opportunities to discover just how varied one spirit can be.

Come thirsty. Leave knowing your Rum from your Ron and your Rhum.

title: Midweek Cheese and Wine Evening at City Centre
description:
Break up the week with an evening of indulgence at our Cheese and Wine Tasting, hosted at Loki Great Western Arcade. Settle into our warm, welcoming space and enjoy a relaxed night of flavour exploration, great conversation, and expertly paired wines and cheeses.

Led by our knowledgeable host, you’ll taste seven wines from around the world, each matched with an artisan cheese chosen to showcase balance, contrast, and harmony. Expect crisp whites, vibrant rosés, characterful reds, and a sweet finale, along with a few pairings that may surprise you.

Whether you’re new to wine or already a curious enthusiast, this tasting offers the perfect mix of learning and enjoyment.

What to Expect at Our Midweek Cheese and Wine Tasting

title: Fine Wine Tasting – Burgundy
description:
Burgundy’s reputation rests on two grapes: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Yet within this celebrated French region, they reveal an extraordinary range of styles, shaped by individual vineyards, the people who tend them and the decisions made in the cellar.

Our Fine Burgundy: Pinot Noir & Chardonnay Tasting is an opportunity to explore that diversity through a carefully selected line-up of fine wines. Limited to just 10 guests, this intimate tasting offers time to appreciate each glass, compare styles and discuss the details that make Burgundy so fascinating.

Guided by one of Loki’s wine experts, we’ll explore Chardonnay’s balance of freshness, texture and complexity alongside Pinot Noir’s fragrance, finesse and depth. Expect expressive whites and elegant reds, with each wine chosen to reveal a different aspect of Burgundy’s character.

We’ll unravel the region’s sometimes bewildering labels, explain its vineyard classifications and explore why wines made from the same grape, sometimes only a short distance apart, can taste so different. Along the way, we’ll discuss the influence of vintage, oak and bottle ageing, and what to look for when choosing fine Burgundy.

Expect a thoughtful, relaxed tasting with exceptional wines, lively conversation and plenty of opportunity to ask questions. With only 10 places available, this is a special occasion for anyone keen to get to know Burgundy more closely.

What to Expect at Our Fine Burgundy Tasting

  • Explore a carefully selected line-up of fine Burgundian Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
  • Enjoy an intimate tasting limited to just 10 guests
  • Compare contrasting expressions of Burgundy’s two signature grapes
  • Discover how vineyard location and producer choices shape each wine
  • Make sense of regional, village, Premier Cru and Grand Cru classifications
  • Learn about the influence of vintage, oak and bottle ageing
  • Explore the aromas, textures and complexity that distinguish fine Burgundy
  • Pick up practical advice on choosing, serving and cellaring these wines
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance with plenty of time for questions and discussion

Styles You Might Explore

  • Chablis Chardonnay – focused and fresh, with citrus, mineral character and a distinctive sense of precision
  • Côte de Beaune Chardonnay – expressive whites combining orchard fruit, texture and varying degrees of oak influence
  • Village-Level Pinot Noir – an introduction to the individual character of Burgundy’s villages, from fragrant and delicate to deeper and more structured
  • Premier Cru Burgundy – wines from classified vineyard sites, offering an opportunity to explore greater detail, complexity and length
  • Burgundy with Bottle Age – where included, a chance to discover how fruit develops into more savoury, nutty or earthy flavours over time

  • Collectors looking for inspiration for their next bottle

title: Wine Club: Loki’s Monthly Wine Social
description:
Loki Wine Club: Your New Friday-Night Wine Ritual

Bring a bottle, discover something unexpected and spend Friday evening sharing wine with a room full of fellow wine lovers.

Sometimes, Friday night calls for a glass of wine. And sometimes, you want that glass to come with good company, a little education and the chance to try something completely unexpected.

That is exactly what Loki Wine Club is for.

This relaxed monthly gathering is for people who believe wine is best enjoyed with others. Each guest helps shape the evening by bringing a bottle of wine from home or choosing one from Loki’s shelves. One of our Loki wine experts will host the evening, guide the group through the wines and help uncover the stories, regions, producers and winemaking ideas behind whatever appears on the table.

Together, we will open a collection of bottles, share them around and see where the evening takes us. It is not a formal wine class: there are no tests, no pressure and nobody will ask you to deliver tasting notes in front of the room.

You are very welcome to come on your own, and you do not need to know anybody before you arrive. The whole idea is to meet fellow wine lovers, discover something new and enjoy bottles that are much more fun when opened with other people.

How it works?

  • Bring a bottle you love, something interesting, or something you’d like to learn more about, no corkage fee
  • Share your bottle with the group and taste wines brought by other guests
  • Not sure what to choose? Simply buy your ticket and turn up. Arrive around 10–15 minutes early and we can help you choose something from Loki’s shelves.
  • There is no corkage fee, whether you bring your own bottle or buy one in-store
  • Enjoy a guided introduction and informal discussion led by our in-house expert
  • Discover a wonderfully unpredictable collection of bottles each month
  • Hear the story behind each wine — and share your own, if you would like to
  • Learn from our Loki wine expert and the other wine lovers around the table
  • Taste, share and discuss wine in a relaxed setting with no rigid structure
  • Meet new people in a friendly, welcoming atmosphere
  • Suitable for everyone, whatever your level of wine knowledge

What Should You Bring?

There is no prescribed theme and no bottle budget.

You could bring:

  • A £15 bottle you have recently discovered and absolutely love
  • Something unusual that you would like to understand better
  • A special bottle you have been saving for an occasion that never quite came up
  • An older bottle gathering dust at home that you received as a gift.
  • Something extravagant you have always wanted to share with people who will appreciate it

Perhaps you bought a bottle years ago for a special dinner, but the occasion never arrived. Perhaps the people you planned to open it with have since stopped drinking. This is your opportunity to finally pull the cork and share it with a room full of curious wine lovers.

There is no upper price limit and no pressure to impress. If you are not sure about your bottle, simply drop us an email and we will advise.

Wine Club Rules

  • No pressure to impress, although we may have to turn you down if you bring Blossom Hill, sorry..
  • Know your wine and want to tell everyone the story behind your bottle? Please do. We would love to hear about it.
  • Know absolutely nothing about it and would rather let someone else do the talking? That is completely fine too.
  • Our Loki expert, Melissa, will guide the tasting, talk us through the bottles and help everyone understand what they are drinking. Of course, anyone who thinks they can bring something capable of puzzling her is very welcome to try!
  • The evening is informal and conversational. We will open the bottles, pour them around, compare what everyone has brought and enjoy a completely unpredictable selection of wines together.
  • No two Wine Club evenings will ever be quite the same — because the wines are chosen by you.

Who Is Wine Club For?

    • Anyone looking for a more interesting way to spend a Friday evening over wine
    • People who love wine but do not necessarily know all the technical language
    • Experienced wine drinkers with bottles and stories they would like to share
    • Curious drinkers who want to expand their knowledge without attending a structured class
    • Anyone who enjoys discovering new wines through conversation and sharing
    • Solo guests who would like to meet other wine lovers
    • Anyone with a special, unusual or mysterious bottle waiting to be opened
    • Regulars who want to build a monthly wine ritual, and newcomers just as welcome

What to Expect at Our Valentine’s Wine Tasting

  • Discover wines chosen for personality, character and serious drinkability
  • Explore everything from fresh, elegant whites to juicy, expressive and more structured reds
  • Learn about the grapes, producers and places behind each bottle
  • Compare different styles and discover which wines win you over
  • Pick up simple tasting tips to help you understand what you enjoy and why
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance without any unnecessary wine snobbery
  • Expect a few surprises, plenty of conversation and possibly a new favourite bottle
  • Enjoy a relaxed and sociable Valentine’s tasting that works just as well for friends as it does for couples

  • A silky Pinot Noir or similar light red – elegant, perfumed and charming without trying too hard
  • Something bold and spicy – because every line-up needs a little drama

  • Something sweet to finish – because even we’ll admit Valentine’s Day deserves a little indulgence

The final wines may vary depending on availability, but every bottle will be carefully selected to make the event interesting, varied and thoroughly enjoyable.

Who Should Join the Valentine’s Wine Tasting?

  • Couples looking for a date night that doesn’t involve another three-course set menu
  • Friends celebrating Valentine’s, Galentine’s or simply a mutual appreciation of wine
  • Wine lovers keen to discover a few new favourites
  • Anyone who wants to learn more about wine without things becoming overly serious
  • First dates brave enough to discover each other’s wine preferences

  • Beginners and experienced tasters alike — everyone is welcome

No Grand Romantic Gestures Required

You don’t need to know anything about wine.

You don’t need to arrive with a date.

And you definitely don’t need to pretend you can smell twelve different varieties of rose petal in your glass.

Just bring good company, curiosity and an appetite for discovering something delicious.

After all, finding a wine you love is much easier than dating.

title: Taste of Mexico, by Amuse Booze
description:
Tequila is far more than shots, salt and lime.

Taste of Mexico by Amuse Booze is a guided journey through the world of agave spirits, exploring how raw material, production method and ageing can transform one plant into dramatically different drinks.

Across the tasting, you’ll experience Blanco, Reposado, Añejo and Mezcal side by side, discovering what makes each style distinctive and why agave spirits have become some of the most exciting and expressive drinks in the world.

Expect clear explanations, signature serves, paired nibbles and plenty of stories along the way — all designed to make the world of agave easy to understand, fun to explore and even better to drink.

No salt licking required.

About the Experience

Your Amuse Booze host will guide you through the key styles of tequila and mezcal, using each pour to tell a different part of the agave story.

We’ll begin with the fresh, vibrant character of Blanco, before seeing what happens when tequila spends time in oak with Reposado and Añejo. Then we’ll step beyond tequila into Mezcal, exploring how different agave varieties, traditional production methods and roasting techniques can create something altogether more earthy, smoky and complex.

Along the way, you’ll learn what tequila actually is, why all tequila is agave spirit but not all agave spirit is tequila, and how factors such as ageing, roasting, fermentation and distillation influence what ends up in your glass.

Each style will also be presented through a signature serve and matched with a carefully chosen nibble, showing how flavour combinations can completely change the way a spirit tastes.

Expect plenty of anecdotes, Mexican drinking culture and a few myths busted along the way.

What to Expect

  • Taste Blanco, Reposado, Añejo and Mezcal side by side
  • Discover how ageing changes flavour, texture and complexity in tequila
  • Explore the difference between tequila and mezcal
  • Learn how agave variety, roasting, fermentation and distillation shape the final spirit
  • Enjoy a signature serve built around each style
  • Discover how different garnishes, mixers and serving styles can enhance an agave spirit
  • Enjoy paired nibbles selected to complement each pour
  • Learn about the history and culture behind Mexico’s most famous spirits
  • Pick up useful facts without feeling like you’re sitting through a lecture
  • Expect storytelling, interaction and plenty of Amuse Booze personality throughout

What Will We Be Tasting?

Your journey through agave will include four key styles:

  • Blanco Tequila – fresh and unaged, putting the character of the agave front and centre with bright citrus, pepper, herbs and earthy sweetness
  • Reposado Tequila – gently rested in oak, adding softer vanilla, spice and caramel notes while retaining plenty of fresh agave character
  • Añejo Tequila – aged for longer in barrel, developing richer flavours of oak, dried fruit, spice and toffee with a rounder, more complex texture
  • Mezcal – a broader and more varied agave category, often showing earthy, mineral, herbal and smoky flavours created through traditional production methods

The exact producers and signature serves may vary depending on availability, but each drink will be selected to showcase a distinctive side of Mexico’s agave tradition.

Who Is This For?

  • Cocktail lovers curious about the spirits behind some of their favourite drinks
  • Anyone interested in Mexican food, drinks and culture
  • Groups of friends looking for an interactive and memorable tasting experience
  • Complete beginners — no agave knowledge required

More Than Tequila

Agave spirits are shaped by geography, tradition, time and technique.

A fresh Blanco can be bright, peppery and vibrant. A Reposado might soften into vanilla and spice. Añejo can become rich and luxurious, while Mezcal opens up an entirely different world of earthy, smoky and savoury flavours.

Taste of Mexico brings those contrasts together, giving you the chance to experience the category side by side and understand exactly why each style tastes the way it does.

Four agave spirits. Four signature serves. Plenty of stories.

And hopefully, a completely different idea of what tequila can be.

title: Ready, Steady, Shake, by Amuse Booze
description:

Ready, Steady, Shake by Amuse Booze is a hands-on cocktail masterclass inspired by the spirit of the classic teatime cooking show — only this time, the ingredients are spirits, mixers, garnishes and ice.

Rather than simply following recipes, you’ll be creating your own four-course drinks menu from scratch, shaking, stirring and tasting your way through each stage.

Expect plenty of guidance, a little creative chaos and the chance to find out whether your instincts behind the bar are as good as you think they are.

Your Amuse Booze host will guide you through the building blocks of a great cocktail before handing over the creative reins.

You’ll learn how sweetness, acidity, bitterness, alcohol, dilution and texture work together, then use those principles to start creating your own drinks. We’ll explore how different spirits behave, how to choose complementary flavours and how small changes can completely transform a cocktail.

Along the way, you’ll practise essential techniques including shaking, stirring, building and finishing a drink, as well as discovering how garnishes, glassware and presentation can turn something good into something memorable.

By the end, you won’t just know how to make a cocktail.

You’ll know how to build one.

What to Expect

  • Create your own four-course cocktail menu
  • Learn how to balance sweet, sour, bitter, strong and refreshing flavours
  • Discover how different spirits, mixers and ingredients work together
  • Get hands-on with essential cocktail techniques including shaking and stirring
  • Learn when to shake, when to stir and why it makes a difference
  • Explore flavour matching and how to build a drink from an idea rather than a recipe
  • Discover how dilution, temperature and texture affect the finished cocktail
  • Get creative with garnishes and presentation
  • Taste, tweak and refine your drinks as you go
  • Enjoy expert guidance throughout without losing the fun of experimenting
  • Leave with practical skills you can actually use behind your own bar at home

Your Four-Course Drinks Menu

Rather than being handed four finished cocktails, you’ll build them yourself.

Each round will focus on a different style, technique or flavour challenge, giving you the chance to put what you’ve learned into practice as the session develops.

You might find yourself creating something bright and refreshing, something short and spirit-forward, something adventurous and unexpected, or a final showstopper designed entirely around your own flavour choices.

There are no identical menus here.

Part of the fun is seeing where everyone ends up.

Who Is This For?

  • Cocktail lovers who want to learn how drinks are actually constructed
  • Anyone bored of simply following recipes
  • Groups of friends looking for something hands-on and sociable
  • Curious drinkers who enjoy experimenting with flavour
  • Home bartenders wanting to improve their technique
  • Anyone who has ever watched a cocktail being made and thought, “I could do that”

Ready. Steady. Shake.

This isn’t a demonstration where you sit and watch somebody else do all the interesting bits.

You’ll be behind the shaker.

You’ll choose the flavours.

You’ll make the decisions.

And occasionally, you may discover why professional bartenders measure things.

By the end of the session, you’ll have worked your way through four drinks, developed your own flavour combinations and picked up the skills to start creating cocktails rather than simply copying them.

Ready? Steady? Shake.

title: Pinot Noir Around the World
description:
Few grape varieties reveal where they are grown quite as beautifully as Pinot Noir.

Elegant, expressive and notoriously demanding in the vineyard, Pinot Noir is responsible for some of the world’s most sought-after wines. Yet its character can change dramatically depending on climate, soil, altitude and winemaking — from the perfume and finesse of Burgundy to the vibrant fruit of New Zealand and the precision of the world’s finest cool-climate regions.

For this Pinot Noir Around the World tasting, we’ll explore a carefully curated selection of exceptional Pinot Noirs from some of the grape’s most celebrated homes. Expect benchmark regions, distinguished producers and wines chosen to demonstrate just how diverse this famously transparent grape can be.

Guided by one of Loki’s wine experts, you’ll taste the wines side by side, exploring the subtle differences that separate one region from another. We’ll look at terroir, vineyard conditions, whole-bunch fermentation, oak, extraction and ageing, as well as the qualities that allow the finest Pinot Noir to develop extraordinary complexity over time.

This is a more indulgent tasting designed for anyone who wants to explore Pinot Noir beyond the everyday — discovering why this deceptively delicate grape has inspired such devotion among winemakers, collectors and wine lovers around the world.

What to Expect at Our Pinot Noir Around the World Tasting

  • Taste a selection of Pinot Noir from leading wine regions around the world
  • Compare Old World and New World interpretations side by side
  • Explore the elegance and complexity of Burgundy, Pinot Noir’s historic benchmark
  • Discover outstanding expressions from regions such as Oregon, New Zealand, Germany, Australia and South Africa
  • Learn how climate, altitude, soil and vineyard location influence Pinot Noir
  • Explore the impact of whole-bunch fermentation, extraction, oak and bottle ageing
  • Discover how Pinot Noir can range from delicate and perfumed to deeper, darker and more structured
  • Learn to recognise characteristics such as red fruit, florals, spice, earthiness and savoury development
  • Compare prestigious producers and appellations in a relaxed, guided setting
  • Gain a deeper understanding of what makes the finest Pinot Noir so distinctive — and why it can command such extraordinary prices

What Might We Be Pouring?

The final line-up will be confirmed nearer the tasting, but may include wines from:

  • Burgundy, France – the historic reference point for Pinot Noir, producing wines renowned for perfume, finesse, complexity and extraordinary expression of individual vineyards
  • Willamette Valley, Oregon – elegant and beautifully balanced, often combining ripe red fruit with freshness, spice and an earthy, savoury edge
  • Central Otago, New Zealand – vibrant and expressive, with generous cherry and dark berry fruit balanced by freshness and fine structure
  • Germany – known locally as Spätburgunder, producing increasingly refined Pinot Noir with bright fruit, minerality and delicate savoury complexity
  • Tasmania or Victoria, Australia – cool-climate Pinot Noir combining purity of fruit with spice, freshness and elegant structure
  • South Africa – particularly exciting in cooler coastal regions, where Pinot Noir can show wonderful perfume, red fruit and restrained, savoury character
  • A special or mature expression – an opportunity to experience how high-quality Pinot Noir evolves with age, developing greater savoury, earthy and complex tertiary character

The final wines will depend on vintage and availability, with every bottle selected to represent an exceptional expression of Pinot Noir and its place of origin.

Who Should Join the Pinot Noir Around the World Tasting?

  • Pinot Noir lovers looking to explore different expressions of the grape
  • Fine-wine enthusiasts interested in comparing benchmark regions
  • Burgundy fans curious about how Pinot Noir performs elsewhere in the world
  • Wine lovers interested in terroir and how strongly one grape can reflect its surroundings
  • Guests keen to explore prestigious producers and higher-quality examples side by side
  • Anyone wanting to understand why Pinot Noir is one of the wine world’s most celebrated — and challenging — varieties
  • Experienced tasters and curious wine drinkers alike; specialist knowledge is not required

One Grape, Many Personalities

Pinot Noir rarely shouts.

Its fascination lies in the detail — the difference between red cherry and darker fruit, fresh flowers and forest floor, silky delicacy and serious structure.

Place the wines next to each other and those differences become even more fascinating.

Pinot Noir Around the World is an opportunity to slow things down, taste some exceptional bottles and explore how one grape can tell completely different stories depending on where in the world it is planted.

One grape. Several remarkable regions. A very good reason to taste them side by side.

title: The Gintleman, by Amuse Booze
description:
Some people host gin tastings. The Gintleman tells stories.

For one special return, Amuse Booze brings back The Gintleman — the quintessential drinks raconteur — for an afternoon of spring and summer gin, sharp anecdotes and nearly two decades spent watching one of the drinks world’s biggest categories completely reinvent itself.

Across four carefully chosen gin serves, you’ll explore where gin is now, how it got here and what has changed after 18 years of distilling, drinking, mixing, marketing and occasionally overcomplicating the humble G&T.

Part tasting, part storytelling and part state-of-the-gin-nation address, this is a relaxed, entertaining look at a category that has changed enormously — told by someone who has been talking about it throughout.

Expect good gin, great stories and absolutely no obligation to pretend every botanical is immediately identifiable.

About the Experience

Over four rounds, The Gintleman will take you through a selection of spring and summer gin serves, each chosen to highlight a different side of the modern gin world.

Along the way, we’ll look back at how the category has evolved over the last 18 years: from the revival of premium London Dry and the explosion of craft distilling to flavoured gin, new botanicals, changing drinking habits and the seemingly endless reinvention of the gin and tonic.

You’ll explore what actually makes one gin different from another, how botanicals influence aroma and flavour, why tonic and garnish matter, and how the best serves allow the spirit itself to shine.

But this isn’t designed as a technical lecture.

The stories matter just as much as the drinks.

What to Expect

  • Enjoy 4 spring and summer gin serves
  • Discover different expressions of gin and the botanicals that shape them
  • Explore how the gin category has changed over the last 18 years
  • Learn what separates London Dry, contemporary and more experimental styles
  • Discover why tonic, dilution, temperature and garnish can dramatically change a serve
  • Explore the rise of craft gin and the trends that have come, gone and occasionally refused to leave
  • Hear stories and anecdotes collected from nearly two decades around the drinks industry
  • Pick up useful gin knowledge without things becoming overly serious
  • Enjoy an entertaining mix of tasting, storytelling and conversation
  • Discover what might be next for one of Britain’s favourite spirits

Four Serves, One Very Long Gin Story

The final line-up will be revealed on the day, but each serve will offer a different perspective on the category.

You might encounter:

  • A classic London Dry – juniper-forward, crisp and unmistakably gin
  • A modern botanical style – showing how distillers have pushed beyond the traditional flavour profile
  • A seasonal spring serve – bright, aromatic and built around fresher flavours
  • A summer gin – refreshing, expressive and made for longer evenings

The drinks may change.

The opinions probably won’t.

Who Is This For?

  • Gin lovers who want to explore the category beyond their usual G&T
  • Anyone interested in how gin has changed over the last two decades

The Gintleman Returns

Eighteen years is a long time in drinks.

Distilleries have opened. Styles have changed. Botanicals have multiplied. Pink gin happened.

Through it all, The Gintleman has been there to taste it, talk about it and collect a fair few stories along the way.

This one-off return brings together four seasonal gin serves, 18 years of perspective and an afternoon of the anecdotes and expertise that built The Gintleman name in the first place.

Gin has changed.

The stories have only got better.

title: Wine Club: Loki’s Monthly Wine Social
description:
Loki Wine Club: Your New Friday-Night Wine Ritual

Bring a bottle, discover something unexpected and spend Friday evening sharing wine with a room full of fellow wine lovers.

Sometimes, Friday night calls for a glass of wine. And sometimes, you want that glass to come with good company, a little education and the chance to try something completely unexpected.

That is exactly what Loki Wine Club is for.

This relaxed monthly gathering is for people who believe wine is best enjoyed with others. Each guest helps shape the evening by bringing a bottle of wine from home or choosing one from Loki’s shelves. One of our Loki wine experts will host the evening, guide the group through the wines and help uncover the stories, regions, producers and winemaking ideas behind whatever appears on the table.

Together, we will open a collection of bottles, share them around and see where the evening takes us. It is not a formal wine class: there are no tests, no pressure and nobody will ask you to deliver tasting notes in front of the room.

You are very welcome to come on your own, and you do not need to know anybody before you arrive. The whole idea is to meet fellow wine lovers, discover something new and enjoy bottles that are much more fun when opened with other people.

How it works?

  • Bring a bottle you love, something interesting, or something you’d like to learn more about, no corkage fee
  • Share your bottle with the group and taste wines brought by other guests
  • Not sure what to choose? Simply buy your ticket and turn up. Arrive around 10–15 minutes early and we can help you choose something from Loki’s shelves.
  • There is no corkage fee, whether you bring your own bottle or buy one in-store
  • Enjoy a guided introduction and informal discussion led by our in-house expert
  • Discover a wonderfully unpredictable collection of bottles each month
  • Hear the story behind each wine — and share your own, if you would like to
  • Learn from our Loki wine expert and the other wine lovers around the table
  • Taste, share and discuss wine in a relaxed setting with no rigid structure
  • Meet new people in a friendly, welcoming atmosphere
  • Suitable for everyone, whatever your level of wine knowledge

What Should You Bring?

There is no prescribed theme and no bottle budget.

You could bring:

  • A £15 bottle you have recently discovered and absolutely love
  • Something unusual that you would like to understand better
  • A special bottle you have been saving for an occasion that never quite came up
  • An older bottle gathering dust at home that you received as a gift.
  • Something extravagant you have always wanted to share with people who will appreciate it

Perhaps you bought a bottle years ago for a special dinner, but the occasion never arrived. Perhaps the people you planned to open it with have since stopped drinking. This is your opportunity to finally pull the cork and share it with a room full of curious wine lovers.

There is no upper price limit and no pressure to impress. If you are not sure about your bottle, simply drop us an email and we will advise.

Wine Club Rules

  • No pressure to impress, although we may have to turn you down if you bring Blossom Hill, sorry..
  • Know your wine and want to tell everyone the story behind your bottle? Please do. We would love to hear about it.
  • Know absolutely nothing about it and would rather let someone else do the talking? That is completely fine too.
  • Our Loki expert, Melissa, will guide the tasting, talk us through the bottles and help everyone understand what they are drinking. Of course, anyone who thinks they can bring something capable of puzzling her is very welcome to try!

  • No two Wine Club evenings will ever be quite the same — because the wines are chosen by you.

    • Anyone looking for a more interesting way to spend a Friday evening over wine
    • People who love wine but do not necessarily know all the technical language
    • Experienced wine drinkers with bottles and stories they would like to share
    • Curious drinkers who want to expand their knowledge without attending a structured class

    • Regulars who want to build a monthly wine ritual, and newcomers just as welcome

title: The Signore Spritz Show, by Amuse Booze
description:
There is far more to the Spritz than Aperol.

The Signore Spritz Show by Amuse Booze is an afternoon celebration of aperitivo culture, exploring how one simple idea — bitters, bubbles and soda — became one of the world’s most recognisable drinks.

Across the session, you’ll taste your way through the past, present and future of the Spritz, discovering a range of bitter, botanical and aperitivo-led flavours alongside carefully matched sparkling wines including Prosecco, Cava and Crémant.

Each round brings together an aperitivo, bubbles and soda in a different way, giving you a dual tasting experience that explores not only the finished Spritz, but also how the individual components shape aroma, flavour, texture and balance.

Expect bright flavours, plenty of fizz, fascinating stories and a suitably relaxed afternoon atmosphere.

About the Experience

Your Amuse Booze host will guide you through the history and evolution of the Spritz, from its roots in northern Italy to the colourful, highly creative category it has become today.

You’ll discover how bitterness, sweetness, acidity and carbonation work together, why different sparkling wines can completely change a serve, and how sodas and mixers play a much bigger role than simply topping up the glass.

Along the way, you’ll taste contrasting aperitivo styles, compare Prosecco, Cava and Crémant, and explore how modern producers are taking the Spritz in new directions.

Selected matched nibbles will accompany the experience, helping to highlight the flavours in each serve and bringing a little extra aperitivo spirit to the afternoon.

What to Expect

  • Explore the past, present and future of the Spritz
  • Taste a range of aperitivo styles beyond the familiar Aperol serve
  • Compare sparkling wines including Prosecco, Cava and Crémant
  • Discover how different bubbles change the character of a Spritz
  • Explore the role of soda, bitterness, sweetness and acidity in building balance
  • Taste contrasting serves side by side to understand how each component works
  • Learn the story of aperitivo culture and how an afternoon ritual became a global phenomenon
  • Discover modern and more adventurous interpretations of the classic Spritz
  • Enjoy selected matched nibbles alongside the tasting
  • Expect plenty of stories, fizz and Amuse Booze personality throughout

What Might Be in Your Glass?

The exact line-up will form part of the show, but you can expect a journey through very different interpretations of the Spritz.

You might encounter:

  • The Classic – bright, bittersweet and refreshing, showing why the traditional aperitivo formula works so well
  • A Prosecco-led Spritz – soft, fruity and lively, built around Italy’s most famous sparkling wine
  • A Cava variation – drier and more structured, giving the drink a different kind of freshness and texture
  • A Crémant serve – elegant and refined, showing how traditional-method bubbles can completely change the style
  • The New Wave – contemporary aperitifs, unexpected botanicals and flavours pointing towards where the Spritz category might go next

The final serves may vary depending on availability, but each will be selected to showcase a different side of the Spritz and aperitivo world.

Who Is This For?

  • Spritz lovers ready to explore beyond Aperol
  • Fans of Prosecco, Cava and Crémant
  • Anyone who enjoys aperitivo culture and relaxed afternoon drinking
  • Cocktail lovers curious about bitterness, balance and flavour
  • Groups of friends looking for a fun and sociable afternoon experience
  • Anyone interested in discovering new aperitifs and sparkling wines
  • Complete beginners — no cocktail or wine knowledge required

More Than Aperol

The Spritz looks simple.

A little aperitivo. A little fizz. A little soda.

But change any one of those ingredients and you can create something completely different.

The Signore Spritz Show pulls the drink apart and puts it back together again, giving you the chance to compare aperitifs, sparkling wines and sodas side by side before seeing how they come together in the glass.

It’s bright, bitter, bubbly and unapologetically made for the afternoon.

Salute.

title: Mediterranean Islands Wine Tasting
description:
Some of the most exciting wines in the Mediterranean come from places surrounded by sea.

For this special Mediterranean Islands Wine Tasting, we’re leaving the mainland behind and travelling through a selection of remarkable island wine regions, where volcanic soils, coastal winds, intense sunshine and centuries-old grape varieties create wines with real personality.

Across the tasting, we’ll explore seven carefully selected wines from islands such as Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica, Santorini, Crete, Mallorca and Cyprus, discovering just how different island wine can be. Expect everything from crisp, salty whites and aromatic native grapes to elegant reds, volcanic wines and richer Mediterranean styles.

Guided by one of Loki’s wine experts, you’ll discover how isolation has helped preserve indigenous grape varieties, why island vineyards often develop such distinctive identities, and how sea breezes, altitude, heat and ancient soils shape what ends up in the glass.

Expect sunshine in wine form, plenty of unfamiliar grapes and a few bottles that may completely change the way you think about Mediterranean wine.

What to Expect at Our Mediterranean Islands Wine Tasting

  • Taste seven wines from Mediterranean islands
  • Explore a range of styles, from crisp mineral whites to structured and aromatic reds
  • Discover islands including Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica, Santorini, Crete, Mallorca and Cyprus
  • Get to know fascinating indigenous grape varieties that rarely appear anywhere else
  • Explore the influence of volcanic soils, coastal winds, altitude and intense Mediterranean sunshine
  • Discover why island vineyards can produce wines with such distinctive freshness and character
  • Learn how traditional winemaking and modern producers are working side by side
  • Compare wines from very different islands and climates
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance in a relaxed and sociable atmosphere
  • Discover new regions, grapes and producers well beyond the familiar Mediterranean classics

Example Wines You Might Taste

  • Etna Bianco, Sicily – fresh and mineral, often combining citrus, herbs and a distinctive volcanic edge
  • Vermentino di Gallura, Sardinia – aromatic and vibrant, with citrus, Mediterranean herbs and a subtle salty character
  • Assyrtiko, Santorini – intense, bone-dry and famously mineral, with sharp citrus, high acidity and unmistakable volcanic character
  • Vidiano, Crete – textured and aromatic, with ripe stone fruit, citrus and plenty of freshness
  • Niellucciu or Sciaccarellu, Corsica – elegant and savoury, with red fruit, herbs and a distinctly Mediterranean personality
  • Mantonegro, Mallorca – juicy, fragrant and often slightly spicy, showing the softer and more charming side of island reds
  • Commandaria or another Cypriot style – rich, historic and distinctive, offering a completely different expression of Mediterranean island winemaking

Who Should Join the Mediterranean Islands Wine Tasting?

  • Wine lovers looking to discover something beyond the usual regions
  • Fans of Mediterranean wine who want to explore lesser-known islands and grapes
  • Anyone curious about volcanic wines and indigenous grape varieties
  • Travellers who enjoy discovering wine through place and culture
  • Fans of fresh, mineral whites and characterful Mediterranean reds
  • Curious drinkers looking for new producers and unusual styles
  • Beginners and experienced tasters alike — relaxed, informative and full of discovery
  • Friends and couples looking for a tasting with a slightly more adventurous feel

Wine With an Island Accent

Island wines often taste like nowhere else.

They can be salty, smoky, floral, herbal, mineral, sun-drenched or incredibly fresh — sometimes all at once.

That is what makes them so fascinating.

This tasting is a chance to travel around the Mediterranean without leaving your seat, discovering how different islands have developed their own grapes, traditions and unmistakable sense of place.

Seven wines. Several islands.

No ferry required.

title: Tot to Tiki, by Amuse Booze
description:
From sailors’ rations and sugar plantations to beach bars, Daiquiris and full-blown Tiki extravagance, rum has one of the most colourful stories in the drinks world.

Tot to Tiki by Amuse Booze takes you on a journey through that story, following rum from its early Caribbean beginnings to the remarkably diverse spirit we know today. Across four timeline-inspired serves, you’ll discover how one spirit evolved into three distinct traditions — Rum, Ron and Rhum — shaped by different islands, empires, ingredients and approaches to production.

Expect history without the history lesson, plenty of fascinating facts and four very different drinks designed to bring each chapter of the story to life.

Pirates may feature.

Tiny umbrellas are not guaranteed.

About the Experience

Across four rounds, your Amuse Booze host will take you through key moments in rum’s evolution, with each drink representing a different chapter in its story.

We’ll explore how sugarcane became spirit, why British, Spanish and French Caribbean islands developed such different styles, and how everything from naval traditions and colonial trade to Prohibition and post-war Tiki culture helped shape the way we drink rum today.

Along the way, you’ll discover the difference between molasses-based rum and fresh sugarcane Rhum Agricole, explore contrasting ageing and production styles, and taste how geography and history have created an extraordinary range of flavours.

Expect stories, interactive moments and plenty of Amuse Booze fun along the way.

What to Expect

  • Enjoy 4 timeline-inspired rum serves, each representing a key chapter in rum history
  • Travel from the earliest Caribbean spirits through naval rum, classic cocktails and the rise of Tiki culture
  • Discover the differences between Rum, Ron and Rhum
  • Explore British, Spanish and French-influenced rum traditions
  • Learn how molasses, fresh sugarcane juice, fermentation and ageing influence flavour
  • Discover how piracy, naval history, colonial trade and Caribbean culture became intertwined with rum
  • Taste a variety of styles, from bold and characterful to smooth, elegant and tropical
  • Pick up plenty of strange, surprising and genuinely useful rum facts
  • Experience an interactive tasting that’s informative without taking itself too seriously

Where Will the Journey Take You?

The exact drinks will form part of the experience, but your journey could include:

  • The Early Tot – exploring rum’s beginnings in the Caribbean and the fiery spirits that became part of everyday naval life
  • Rum – the British-influenced tradition, often associated with Jamaica, Barbados and other former British Caribbean islands, where richer and more characterful styles developed
  • Ron – the smoother Spanish-influenced tradition found in places such as Cuba, Puerto Rico and beyond, where ageing and blending helped create a more refined style
  • Rhum – the distinctive French Caribbean tradition, particularly Rhum Agricole, produced directly from fresh sugarcane juice rather than molasses
  • The Cocktail Revolution – how drinks such as the Daiquiri helped take Caribbean spirits around the world
  • Tiki Takes Over – tropical escapism, elaborate cocktails and the colourful mid-century drinking culture that turned rum into the star of the show

The final four drinks will be selected to tell the story of rum through the glass, so expect a few surprises along the way.

Who Is This For?

  • Rum lovers wanting to explore the spirit beyond their usual bottle
  • Cocktail fans curious about the history behind classic rum serves
  • Anyone who has wondered what actually separates Rum, Ron and Rhum
  • Curious drinkers who enjoy history when it comes with something good in the glass
  • Groups of friends looking for a fun and different tasting experience
  • Whisky or brandy drinkers interested in exploring aged rum
  • Complete beginners — no previous rum knowledge required

From Tot to Tiki

Rum’s story isn’t really one story at all.

It’s sailors and sugarcane. Pirates and plantations. Caribbean islands separated by language and empire. Naval rations, elegant Cuban cocktails and enormous Tiki creations decorated with enough fruit to qualify as lunch.

Tot to Tiki brings those stories together through four drinks, four moments in time and plenty of opportunities to discover just how varied one spirit can be.

Come thirsty. Leave knowing your Rum from your Ron and your Rhum.

description:

Led by our knowledgeable host, you’ll taste seven wines from around the world, each matched with an artisan cheese chosen to showcase balance, contrast, and harmony. Expect crisp whites, vibrant rosés, characterful reds, and a sweet finale, along with a few pairings that may surprise you.

title: Fine Wine Tasting – South Africa
description:
South Africa’s fine wines bring together centuries of winemaking heritage and a restless spirit of discovery. From old-vine Chenin Blanc to elegant Chardonnay, expressive Syrah and refined Cabernet blends, the Cape offers wines of remarkable depth, freshness and individuality.

Our Fine Wine South Africa Tasting is an opportunity to explore this diversity through a carefully selected line-up of premium South African wines. Limited to just 10 guests, this intimate tasting gives you time to appreciate each glass, compare styles and discover the vineyards and producers behind them.

Guided by one of Loki’s wine experts, we’ll explore how ocean breezes, mountain slopes and contrasting vineyard soils shape the wines of the Cape. Regions such as Stellenbosch, Swartland and Hemel-en-Aarde will provide a starting point for discovering the different expressions of familiar grapes.

Along the way, we’ll discuss South Africa’s treasured old vines, the creativity behind its distinctive blends and how oak and bottle ageing contribute to a wine’s development. We’ll also share practical advice on choosing, serving and cellaring these wines, whether you’re searching for a special bottle to open now or something to enjoy in years to come.

Expect outstanding wines, fascinating producer stories and relaxed conversation in a small-group setting. With only 10 places available, this is a special opportunity to discover the quality and character of South African fine wine.

What to Expect at Our Fine Wine South Africa Tasting

  • Taste a carefully selected line-up of fine South African wines
  • Enjoy an intimate tasting limited to just 10 guests
  • Explore regions such as Stellenbosch, Swartland and Hemel-en-Aarde
  • Discover premium expressions of Chenin Blanc, Chardonnay, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon
  • Learn how ocean influence, altitude and vineyard location shape regional styles
  • Explore the importance of old vines and the concentration they can bring
  • Discover the creativity behind South Africa’s distinctive white and red blends
  • Understand how oak and bottle ageing influence flavour, texture and complexity
  • Pick up practical advice on choosing, serving and cellaring these wines
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance with plenty of time for questions and discussion

Styles You Might Explore

  • Old-Vine Chenin Blanc – textured and layered, with orchard fruit, citrus and a balance of richness and freshness
  • Cape White Blend – a distinctive combination of grapes, bringing together aromatic detail, depth and texture
  • Hemel-en-Aarde Chardonnay – poised and expressive, combining citrus and stone fruit with freshness and carefully judged oak
  • Hemel-en-Aarde Pinot Noir – fragrant and elegant, with red berry fruit, savoury complexity and fine structure
  • Swartland Syrah – expressive and characterful, with dark berries, pepper, herbs and a savoury edge
  • Stellenbosch Cabernet Sauvignon or Bordeaux-Style Blend – structured and complex, with cassis, cedar and the potential to develop beautifully with age
  • Fine Pinotage – an opportunity to explore South Africa’s signature grape in a carefully crafted style, with depth, fruit and savoury detail

title: Raise a Glass to the Grill: BBQ Wine Tasting
description:
There’s more to choosing wine for a barbecue than reaching for the biggest red on the shelf. From crisp whites with grilled fish to juicy reds alongside smoky vegetables and richly flavoured meats, the right bottle can make your summer spread even more delicious.

For our Wines for the BBQ Tasting, we’ll explore seven carefully selected wines to inspire your next outdoor get-together. Expect refreshing whites, versatile rosé and reds ranging from bright and juicy to bold and spicy, with plenty of ideas for matching them to whatever’s cooking on the grill.

Guided by one of Loki’s wine experts, you’ll discover how smoke, char, marinades and sauces influence a wine pairing. We’ll explain why a wine that works beautifully with a simply grilled steak might need a different approach when sweet barbecue sauce or chilli enters the picture.

Along the way, we’ll share practical tips for serving wine outdoors, keeping bottles at the right temperature and choosing a few versatile styles to please a crowd. Whether your barbecue centres on burgers, seafood or vegetables, you’ll leave with plenty of inspiration for your summer table.

Expect delicious wines, useful pairing advice and a relaxed tasting that will help you become the most popular person at the next barbecue.

What to Expect at Our Wines for the BBQ Tasting

  • Taste seven carefully selected wines suited to summer barbecues
  • Explore refreshing whites, versatile rosé and a variety of reds
  • Discover pairing ideas for grilled meat, fish and vegetables
  • Learn how smoke, char and seasoning affect your choice of wine
  • Explore how to approach sweet sauces, spicy marinades and rich flavours
  • Find lighter reds that taste delicious with a little chill
  • Pick up practical tips for serving wine outdoors
  • Discover versatile bottles for sharing with friends
  • Enjoy expert-led guidance in a relaxed and sociable atmosphere

Example Wines You Might Taste

  • Dry Rosé – refreshing and versatile, with red berry fruit that suits a varied barbecue spread
